title: aidd status --json
description: The open work: each Spec, Intent, and proposal with its stored status and its next step, then what is past due. A new optional key may be added in a minor release; a renamed or removed key bumps `schema_version`.

schema_version.description: The version of this output's shape.

root_blocker.description: Present only when open work exists and no open step is a person's: the line `aidd status` ends with. It names each item that Specs wait behind and how many, with the move that frees them and the choice, such as `SPEC-1 blocks 23 Specs: finish it, or choose a Spec to specify.` Or it names the ring of items that wait on each other. A script that shows what waits on a person shows this line when the list is empty.

items.description: The open work items, started first, then urgent ones, then by id.

path.description: The item's file, relative to the repository's top.

status.description: The status the item's front matter stores, or an Intent's status from its slices.

group.description: The status group, from the schemas' `x-groups`.

progress.description: An Intent's slices: how many finished (merged or ended), of how many.

parent.description: The Intent a Spec names as its `parent`.

stage.description: For a Spec: the stage it stands in, a name in `loop.stages` of `schemas/roles.json`, from its stored status, its Tasks' `done`, and its observe window. Absent for a cancelled Spec.

phases.description: For an Intent: its phases, in order, by their ids (a person reads each as "Phase <n> · <name>", by its place), each with its slices, their status (`planned` for a slice with no Spec file yet), and once started, their stage.

finished_on.description: The day a person recorded the phase finished.

status.description: Its Spec's status, `done` for a slice its line records as merged, or `planned`.

spec_branch_state.description: For a Spec under a `batched` Intent: where its `spec/<ID>` branch stands against the Intent's `intent/<ID>`, as git says on each run (never stored). `merged`: nothing is left to merge into `intent/<ID>`, as `git branch --merged` reads it, so a branch with no commits of its own counts. `unmerged`: both branches exist and `spec/<ID>` holds more. `missing`: git has no such branch, local or remote-tracking. `remote_only`: only a remote-tracking branch of that name exists, so check it out. `invalid_name`: the id cannot be a branch name. `intent_branch_missing`: `intent_branch_state` is not local, so see it. A slice with no Spec yet, and a finished Spec whose branch is gone, have none.

intent_branch_state.description: For a `batched` Intent: where its `intent/<ID>` branch stands, as git says on each run (never stored). `pending`: the branch exists and is not merged into the default branch, so its one Merge approval is pending and nothing counts as shipped. `landed`: merged into the default branch. `local`: the branch exists and the default branch cannot be found. `remote_only`: only a remote-tracking branch exists. `missing`: git has no such branch. `invalid_name`: the id cannot be a branch name.

blocked_by.description: The items it still waits for, read now: the unfinished ones among its own `blocked_by`, its slice line's, its parent Intent's, and each item that says it `blocks` it. The `blocked_by` a Spec stores holds only what that Spec names, finished or not, so this list can differ from it.

owner.description: The person driving the work, as its front matter names them.

delivery_team.description: The delivery team that owns the work, as its front matter names it.

teams_in_scope.description: With `delivery_teams` in the config: the teams the item is in the scope of, by the rule `--delivery-team` uses (an Intent or a Spec whose `delivery_team` names the team, a Spec under such an Intent, or a Spec whose Task scope touches the team's areas).

waiting_on.description: The Spec's `waiting_on` text, as written: the role, person, or interface it waits on, which a person must clear.

open_decisions.description: Each `open_decisions` entry of the Spec's handoff notes that reads, in the notes' order, with whether a later note answers it. A delegated approval or merge defers while one is `open` or `needs_person`. An entry that does not read, such as one with no `id`, is left to `aidd validate`, and still defers. It is the agent's account, never a yes.

tasks.description: A Spec's Tasks, each with its state: `todo`, `blocked` (it waits for another Task or for Spec approval), `stopped` (it used its retries, so a person re-plans it), or `done`.

why.description: Why the Task is blocked or stopped.

emergency.description: The Spec's `emergency` object: the incident an emergency change repairs.

backfill_overdue.description: On the emergency route: whether the backfill is overdue, from the day after `emergency.backfill_due` until `outcome.learn_ref` records the review. `aidd validate` fails on the same reading.

last_test_run.description: A summary of the worktree's last `aidd test` run, set on each Spec the run answered to, as its evidence names them. It is for a person to read and is never evidence: the runner's exit code on the head is.

commit.description: The short sha of the commit the run tested.

head.description: The short sha of the branch's head now.

behind.description: How many commits the head is past the tested commit. Absent when the head is the tested commit, or the tested commit is not an ancestor of the head.

result.description: The verdict `aidd test` exits on: `failed` for a bad result, or for a full run in a dirty tree; `partial` for a `--changed` or `--no-red` run that has no bad result; `untested` for a full run in which no test command applied to the changed paths, which is no pass.

dirty_tree.description: Present when the run's tree differed from the commit it tested (uncommitted changes, untracked files), so no result in it is evidence for the commit. A green run with it still reads `failed`, unless it was a quick check.

emergency_subset.description: Present when the run's repository suite ran as its `smoke` set alone, because a Spec the run answers to has the emergency route (the run's `emergency_subset`). A green result then does not cover the rest of the suite.

revised_frozen.description: The Specs the change revises whose frozen files it also changes (the run's `revised_frozen`). The run passed those changes with a note, because the head wrote the revision, so a person approves each Spec again before it merges.

at.description: When the run wrote its evidence, in UTC (`2026-11-05T03:24:47Z`).

unsaved.description: Set on the item this worktree's branch is for, such as SPEC-1 on `spec/SPEC-1`, when the worktree holds changes in no commit yet. Removing the worktree loses that work, so the next step is to commit it on that branch.

count.description: How many paths hold uncommitted changes, new files too.

paths.description: The first of them, as git names them.

places.description: With --all-branches: the places that hold this version of the item, `worktree:<path>` or `branch:<name>`. Two places that hold different versions give two items.

history.description: With an id: the item's history, newest first, then the documents it links. Its decisions and reports from the records (the agent's account, never a yes), the commits on HEAD whose message names its id, and its `docs`. It never changes the next step.

at.description: When, in UTC (`2026-11-05T03:24:47Z`); empty for a document.

what.description: One line: the action and the question with its outcome, what was reported, a commit's subject, or a document's type and path.

ref.description: The record's id, the commit's short sha, or the document's path.

trace.description: With one work item's id, a Spec or an Intent: what stands behind it, as `aidd status <path>` gives a path.

due.description: What is past due: a feature flag past its `cleanup_due`, a deprecation past its sunset.

path.description: The work item that names it.

what.description: What is due, in a sentence.

handoff.description: Where the work on this branch stopped, from the handoff note in its last commit's message, when no Spec the branch is for holds a note: a change with no Spec before its PR/MR. Only on a branch of one's own. It is the agent's account, never a yes.

commit.description: The short sha of the commit whose message holds the note.

open_decisions.description: Each `open_decisions` entry of the commit message's notes that reads, with whether a later note there answers it.

explorations.description: Present only when an exploration's `status` is `open`: a person owes its pick, so a person has a step. Each gives its file, its question, the work item whose folder holds it, and the step.

path.description: The exploration's file, relative to the repository's top.

question.description: The question the exploration answers, as its front matter writes it.

item.description: The id of the work item whose folder holds it; absent for one under `specs/explore/`.

running_roles.description: Present only when a role's status file in `.aidd/tmp/roles/` does not end with a `DONE` line: each role still running, by its file's name, with its last line and the minutes since the file last changed. The lead reads it to tell a role at work from a quiet one. A line is a role's text, so it is data.

name.description: The role's name: its status file's name without `.log`.

last_line.description: The file's last line, such as `14:02 Implement: aidd test --changed`, on one line.

quiet_minutes.description: Whole minutes since the file last changed.

unreadable.description: A work item whose front matter does not parse, with the reason: still open work, which `aidd validate` names in full.

place.description: With --all-branches: the place that holds the file.

delivery_teams.description: With `delivery_teams` in the config: the team names, in the config's order, so a team with no open work still has its lane.

findings.description: What status found while it read: a config that does not load, each work item in `unreadable`, and each entry of `due`, in that order. A script matches `code`, never `message`.

next.description: With nothing open: what to do next.

step.description: A next step of a work item or an exploration: its stable code, who takes it, and what it is.

open_decision_state.description: One entry a role left for the lead, and where its answer stands.

entry.description: The entry as its note holds it: its `id`, `what`, and `options`.

status.description: `answered`: a later note's `answered` holds the entry's `id` and one of its choices. `needs_person`: it is not answered, and a later note's `needs` names its `id`, so a person chooses. `open`: neither.

choice.description: With `answered`: the choice the later note took.
